provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Choral welcome
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing the welcome round with correct rhythm.
The pupils should be able to clap in harmony with the song.

Introduction:
We love to start our day with songs.
We will sing our special welcome song today.

Content:
Stand in a circle.
Sing the welcome round together.
Clap your hands on the beat.
Add harmony claps after each verse.

Class activity:
Form a circle.
Sing the welcome song while clapping.
Pass a smile around the circle.

Evaluation questions:
What song do we sing at the start of class?
When do we clap our hands?
Can you show me a harmony clap?

Summary:
We sing and clap together every day.

topics.title: Twinkle twinkle with verses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite new verses to Twinkle Twinkle.
The pupils should be able to perform a solo or duet.

Introduction:
We know Twinkle Twinkle Little Star.
Today we will add new verses.

Content:
Recite the original Twinkle Twinkle.
Add verses about the moon and sun.
Take turns singing solo parts.
Sing duets with a partner.

Class activity:
Sit in pairs.
Practice new verses together.
Take turns being the star and the moon.

Evaluation questions:
What is the first line of Twinkle Twinkle?
What new verse did we learn?
Can you sing a solo?

Summary:
We can sing Twinkle Twinkle many ways.

topics.title: Counting rhymes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite counting rhymes.
The pupils should be able to count using props.

Introduction:
We count every day in class.
Today we count with fun rhymes.

Content:
Learn One Two Buckle My Shoe.
Practice Ten Green Bottles.
Use fingers to count numbers.
Use bottles or blocks as props.

Class activity:
Place ten bottles in a row.
Sing Ten Green Bottles.
Remove one bottle each time.

Evaluation questions:
What rhyme counts to ten?
What rhyme counts to five?
How many bottles are left?

Summary:
Counting is fun with rhymes and props.

topics.title: Animal rhymes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to sing animal rhymes.
The pupils should be able to make animal sounds.

Introduction:
We love animals in Nigeria.
Today we sing about farm animals.

Content:
Sing Old MacDonald Had a Farm.
Learn Five Little Ducks.
Make animal sounds like quack and moo.
Sing the chorus together.

Class activity:
Move like different animals.
Make animal sounds as we sing.
Take turns leading the animal chorus.

Evaluation questions:
What animal says quack quack?
What animal says moo?
Can you sing Old MacDonald?

Summary:
Animal rhymes are fun to sing and act out.

topics.title: Action rhymes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform action rhymes.
The pupils should be able to follow leader movements.

Introduction:
We use our bodies in music class.
Today we sing and move.

Content:
Sing Head Shoulders Knees and Toes.
Sing If You're Happy and You Know It.
Touch body parts as we sing.
Clap and stomp to the beat.

Class activity:
Stand in a circle.
Sing action rhymes together.
One child leads the movements.
Follow the leader around the circle.

Evaluation questions:
Which body part touches your head?
What action do we do when happy?
Can you follow the leader?

Summary:
Action rhymes help us move and sing.

topics.title: Nursery rap
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap a simple beat.
The pupils should be able to rap the alphabet.

Introduction:
We can rap in music class.
Today we rap our ABCs.

Content:
Clap a steady beat like a drum.
Rap the alphabet letters.
Speak clearly and fast.
Perform in groups of four.

Class activity:
Sit in groups.
Practice clapping the beat.
Take turns rapping the alphabet.
Perform for the class.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does a drum make?
Can you rap A to Z?
How many people in your group?

Summary:
Rapping the alphabet is fun with beats.

topics.title: Call and response
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to respond to teacher calls.
The pupils should be able to echo rhymes.

Introduction:
We talk back in songs.
Today we play echo games.

Content:
Teacher sings a line.
Class echoes the same line.
Use call and response patterns.
Try longer echo rhymes.

Class activity:
Stand facing the teacher.
Teacher calls out phrases.
Class echoes back with actions.
Move your body as you echo.

Evaluation questions:
What does echo mean?
What does the teacher sing?
What do we sing back?

Summary:
Echo songs help us listen and respond.

topics.title: Rhymes with instruments
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to play shakers and drums.
The pupils should be able to keep the beat.

Introduction:
We make music with instruments.
Today we play and sing.

Content:
Use shakers to make sounds.
Beat drums with your hands.
Play instruments to rhymes.
Keep steady rhythm.

Class activity:
Pass instruments around the circle.
Play while singing Twinkle Twinkle.
Stop and start on teacher's signal.

Evaluation questions:
What sound does a shaker make?
How do you play a drum?
Can you play the steady beat?

Summary:
Instruments make our rhymes sound great.

topics.title: Solo day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform a solo rhyme.
The pupils should be able to encourage others.

Introduction:
We all have special voices.
Today we sing alone.

Content:
Each child chooses a rhyme.
Stand and sing to the class.
Clap for each performer.
Encourage friends with smiles.

Class activity:
Sit in a semi-circle.
One child comes forward.
Perform a favorite rhyme.
Class claps and cheers.

Evaluation questions:
How did you feel singing alone?
What rhyme did you sing?
How did we encourage friends?

Summary:
Everyone has a special singing voice.

topics.title: Rhyme concert
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform all rhymes.
The pupils should be able to give a standing ovation.

Introduction:
We learned many rhymes this term.
Today we show our parents.

Content:
Review all term's rhymes.
Practice standing tall.
Sing with big voices.
Bow at the end.

Class activity:
Set up a small stage.
Perform for parents and friends.
Take a bow after each song.
Give a big clap for everyone.

Evaluation questions:
What songs did we perform?
How did we stand on stage?
What does ovation mean?

Summary:
We shared our music with pride today.
